region: Geneva · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Ravines Wine Cellars was founded in 2001 by Morten Hallgren and his wife, Lisa. Morten grew up on his family’s wine estate in Provence, trained in enology at Montpellier and worked at Château Cos d’Estournel in Bordeaux before becoming chief winemaker at Dr. Konstantin Frank in the Finger Lakes in 1998. The winery began on Keuka Lake, and in 2012 the Hallgrens bought the White Springs production facility and its vineyards on the edge of Geneva, at the north end of Seneca Lake, which is now home to the winery and a second tasting room.

The Dry Riesling is Ravines’ signature wine and is estate grown, from the White Springs and 16 Falls vineyards, using clones 198, 239 and 90. In 2020, an exceptionally warm, sunny season gave very small clusters and high ripeness. Hand-picked grapes were pressed as whole clusters, while the machine-harvested portion had some skin contact before pressing. Everything fermented cool in stainless steel, then aged on light lees through the winter until April.

Wine Review Online found it lively and mouthwatering, with flowers, citrus zest, white peach, fennel and a wet-stone edge, and suggested it has another decade ahead of it. Lime, peach, fennel and pineapple fit that picture of ripe fruit held in tension by acidity. Wine Spectator gave it 90 points, and it is still young enough to reward a few more years in the cellar.
facts: Whole-cluster pressed (hand-picked portion); cool stainless steel fermentation
